input.rationale: Section 15.9 selects Delaware law, which sits at our accepted fallback list. The forum, however, fails the fallback: Section 15.10.1 sends all unresolved Disputes to mandatory, final and binding ICDR arbitration under Section 15.10.2 (seat New York, three-arbitrator tribunal, AAA appellate rules) rather than to the corresponding Delaware courts. The seat is domestic, so this is not walk-away territory, but the courts-over-arbitration element is materially unmet. Our edit keeps Delaware law and every carve-out (executive escalation, IP matters to U.S. federal court, preliminary injunctive relief, Section 7.5.5 Material Impact determination) and simply routes Disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts, making the retained Section 15.10.2 machinery available only by mutual written agreement so no contradictory arbitration right survives.

proposal.summary: Route unresolved Disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts and make the Section 15.10.2 arbitration process available only by mutual written agreement.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that disputes are heard by the courts of the governing-law jurisdiction rather than by mandatory arbitration, so we have sent unresolved Disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the Delaware state and federal courts and made the Section 15.10.2 arbitration process available only if both Parties later agree in writing. Delaware law under Section 15.9 and the executive escalation, intellectual property and preliminary injunctive relief carve-outs are unchanged.

ops.oldText: then such Dispute shall be submitted to the International Centre for Dispute Resolution ("ICDR") for final and binding arbitration pursuant to the arbitration clause set forth in Section 15.10.2.
ops.newText: then such Dispute shall be resolved exclusively by the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware, and each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of those courts.

ops.oldText: Either Party shall have the right to initiate arbitration at any time after the expiration of thirty (30) days after a Dispute is notified to the Executive Officers.
ops.newText: A Dispute may be referred to arbitration under this Section 15.10.2 only if both Parties so agree in writing after the Dispute has arisen.
